obtained.how: USGS report PDF the human had already fetched (public domain), indexed with getsrc --file

bibliography.checked_against: the title page and the report's suggested citation
bibliography.corrections: the title has no comma: "Estimates of growth and mortality of under-yearling smallmouth bass in Spednic Lake from 1970 through 2008"; add the DOI 10.3133/sir20145164; the suggested citation gives "15 p."

claims.claim: Spednic Lake young-of-year 70.7–76.3 mm on 3 Oct 1995 (71–76 mm in autumn)
claims.source_value: 70.7–76.3 mm are the MEANS of four samples (n = 7, 13, 21, 8); individual fish 65–82 mm
claims.conditions: total length; collected at different locations in Spednic Lake on 3 Oct 1995 (Ardnt 1996); the model's estimated range for that year was 80–91 mm. A further 1988 sample (1 Sept, n = 24) averaged 73.0 mm (63–97)
claims.note: write "sample means 71–76 mm" where the paper implies a range of fish

claims.claim: modeled Spednic onset of smallmouth spawning 22 May–4 June, median 28 May
claims.quote: The median (and mean) date for the start of spawning ... was May 28
claims.conditions: modeled from regression-estimated daily mean lake-surface temperatures (from Vanceboro air temperatures), 1970–2008; earliest 22 May (1991, 1998), latest 4 June (2005); mean spawning period 12 days, median end 10 June

claims.claim: about 208 (± 4) days below 10 °C at Spednic Lake
claims.source_value: the estimated starvation period, days from the autumn date of < 10 °C to the spring date of ≥ 10 °C, averaged 208 days (± 4 days, standard deviation), 1970–2008
claims.quote: estimated starvation period ... averaged 208 days (±4 days, standard deviation)
claims.conditions: daily mean lake-surface temperature estimated by regression on air temperature; the regression was applied only from 1 May to 31 October, so the count is the span between the two 10 °C crossings
claims.note: "in Washington County" (§3.5.4) and "~30 km east" (§4.2) are not in the source, which places the lake on the Maine–New Brunswick border in the St. Croix headwaters

claims.claim: spawning starts once daily water exceeds 15 °C (modeled median 28 May)
claims.source_value: spawning is triggered when 15 < Ti ≤ 27 °C and degree-days above 10 °C are < 150, and then delayed by SD = 8.0 − 0.055·DD days
claims.location: p. 4 (PDF p. 12), eqs. 1–2; Fig. 2 on p. 5
claims.quote: Spawning is triggered when Ti is greater than (>) 15 °C
claims.conditions: rules of Shuter et al. (1980) applied to modeled surface temperatures
claims.note: the delay term (up to ~8 days) is why the median spawning date falls a few days after 15 °C

claims.claim: egg and fry mortality is 1 if the minimum temperature in the following 15 days falls below 10 °C and 3.0 − 0.2·Tmin between 10 and 15 °C
claims.conditions: Tmin = minimum daily mean water temperature from spawning date to spawning date + 15 days (assumed fertilization to rise of fry); probability of mortality, from Shuter et al. (1980); also p = 0 for 15–27 °C, 0.33·Tmin − 9 for 27–30 °C, 1 above 30 °C

claims.claim: modeled early mortality exceeded 10 % in 17 of 39 years (1970–2008), reaching 56 %
claims.quote: Mortality exceeded 10 percent for 17 of the years
claims.conditions: for fish spawned on the FIRST day of each year's spawning period; 56.2 % in 1994; no mortality for the last day's spawn in any year

claims.claim: smallmouth growth 0.12·T − 1.7 mm/d at 14.2–25.5 °C, zero below 14.2 °C (Shuter et al. 1980 via Dudley & Trial)
claims.conditions: daily increment of total length (mm) against daily mean water temperature, from Shuter et al. (1980); temperature only: "calculations do not account for lake productivity or food availability"; 1.4 mm/d at 25.5–31.5 °C
claims.note: this rule over-predicted Spednic growth: every measured mean was below the modeled minimum (Table 4: 1995 measured 71–76 vs modeled 80–91 mm; 1988 73 vs 86–95 mm)

claims.claim: at a 208-day winter the Shuter thresholds kill all young smallmouth under 48 mm and none over 92 mm
claims.conditions: winter mortality p = 1 below Cmin, 0 above Cmax, (Cmax − L)/(Cmax − Cmin) between

claims.claim: the measured autumn lengths of 71–76 mm imply a 36–49 % first-winter loss (project arithmetic from their thresholds)
claims.quote: if L was less than Cmin, then p=1; otherwise, p was computed
claims.conditions: the source applies the rule only to its modeled lengths; its own winter mortality estimates (Table 5) are 1–20 % for early-spawned and 19–41 % for late-spawned fish, 4 % and 27 % in 1995
claims.note: the arithmetic checks, but it applies a temperature-only threshold to 3-October sample means; worth saying the authors did not make this calculation

claims.claim: Dudley & Trial record year-class failures after the cold, wet summers of 1986 and 1996
claims.quote: known year-class failures ... caused by cold, wet summers evident in all lakes
claims.conditions: "year-class failure" = age-4 or age-5 bass under 15 % of a 100-fish sample, region-wide (St. Croix and nearby lakes), from Dill et al. (2010)
claims.note: second-hand in the source (Dill et al. 2010); the authors' own model flags 1986, 1994, 1996 and 2004

notes: The report's lake temperatures are modeled, not measured: a regression on daily min/max air temperature fitted at Big Lake (validated ± 0.6 °C at Big Lake and Grand Falls Flowage). Starting length at rise 9.1 mm. The authors stress the modeled lengths are maxima (food not limiting). Also useful: the 1994 year class was 13 % of the 1998 catch (weak).
